title: Classify scratch suffixes as transient residue in scope validator
goal: Prevent .bak/.head/.orig/.rej/.tmp/~ files stranded by timed-out build turns from voiding the iteration's commit — delete them, emit build.scratch.cleaned, and commit the remaining in-scope work.

steps.description: In _build_validate_scope_violations (diff.sh), before the _build_path_in_scope check, test each changed path against a well-known scratch-suffix list (.bak .orig .rej .head .tmp ~). Scratch-suffix paths are rm -f'd from the working tree and cause a build.scratch.cleaned event to be emitted; they are never added to _scope_violations[]. This is the load-bearing DoD item: a stranded .bak/.head sibling no longer voids the iteration.

In _build_compose_instructions (prompt.sh), add one rule line warning that sed -i.bak, git show HEAD:f > f.head, and any other command that leaves a scratch sibling will be treated as an OOS file and deleted — instructing the agent to use sed -i (no suffix) or clean up immediately. This is the cheap independent-rate-reducer described in the issue.

Add test section T_SCRATCH to build-test.sh. The mock simulates a timed-out turn (MOCK_LOOP_RC=2) that edits an in-scope file AND leaves a .bak sibling and a .head sibling stranded. Assertions: (a) diff.patch is non-empty (in-scope work preserved), (b) build.scratch.cleaned event emitted, (c) scope_violation=false in build-summary.json, (d) .bak/.head files absent from working tree after the run. This is the regression test the DoD requires — fails at the merge-base where the scratch-suffix logic does not exist.

notes: summary.sh requires no changes: the scope_violation=false path through _build_write_build_summary already handles the case correctly once diff.sh correctly excludes scratch files from _scope_violations[]. The 'genuine OOS source edit still fails closed' DoD item is covered by the existing T6 test (unchanged) — step-3 adds T_SCRATCH without touching T6.
